## A cut tendon

The biceps is the large muscle at the front of your upper arm. At its lower end, a tendon joins it to a bone of the forearm, just below the elbow.

Imagine that this one tendon is cut. Everything else is healthy: the muscle still contracts when a nerve signals it, the bones are whole and the elbow joint works.

**Predict:** When the biceps contracts, will the forearm lift the school bag?

options.text: Yes. The muscle still contracts, and contracting is what lifts the forearm.
No. The muscle contracts, but with the tendon cut its pull cannot reach the forearm bone.
Yes, and even faster, because a cut tendon no longer holds the muscle back.
No, but only because the signal from the nerve can no longer reach the muscle.
